<file name="/mnt/d/KERJA/PT AGS/RnD/Hackathon/Kirowen_2026/BusLink-Studio/docs/security/review-07.md" language="markdown" >
<content>
# Security review 07 (Kiro `ics-security-reviewer`, read-only)

Date: 2026-11-13. Agent: `.kiro/agents/ics-security-reviewer.md` (shell limited to `git diff`/`git show`, no file writes). Prompt: `docs/kiro-log/prompts/07-security-review.md`. Range: initial commit..`a035e8a`. The raw run output is kept in `review-07-raw.txt`. Fixes are tracked in `review-07-fixes.md`.

**Scope.** The diff is 477 files and about 127k lines, so I did not read all of it. I read the command service, `src-tauri` IPC, the LAN and MQTT modules, Tauri config and capabilities, the Android manifests and plugin, and the export and profile guards. I covered the rest with targeted searches. I changed nothing and ran only read-only git and file/search tools.

## Findings

| Sev | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| medium | `src-tauri/src/control.rs` (`ArmReq`, `control_arm`) | The role comes from the webview request (`role: Role`). Only `Viewer` is refused, so any caller can claim `Commissioner` and unlock comm-config writes (unit ID, baud). The `user` string is also unbounded and goes into the audit row. IEC 62443 IAC/UC is not met, and the audit identity is self-asserted. | Derive the role from a host-side setting (for example a commissioner unlock that needs a deliberate action) and not from IPC. Cap `user` at 64 characters with no control characters. Say in the docs that this is a single-user local app. |
| medium | `src-tauri/src/commands.rs` (`host_of`) and `crates/buslink-core/src/device.rs:69` | `connect_link` accepts any host name or IP for TCP. A host name such as `localhost` is fine, but a loopback IP literal makes `is_loopback_tcp()` true, and `simulated_only` profiles then count as simulator links. A port-forward or serial bridge on `127.0.0.1` pointing at real hardware would let "simulated" control commands reach a real VFD. This breaks the "control only for simulated devices" rule. | Allow the loopback exemption only for the in-process training server (match its exact port or a session-generated marker), not any loopback address. |
| low | `crates/buslink-core/src/lan/routes.rs` (`authenticate`) | The token is accepted as `?t=` on every route and WebSocket, not only on `/`. That puts it in browser history and any proxy logs. `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and the cookie limit the spread, but the surface is wider than needed. | Accept `?t=` only on `GET /`, set the cookie, and redirect to a URL without the token. After that, accept the cookie only. |
| low | `lan/mod.rs` (`LanSnapshot`, `ProfileEntry`) | The snapshot sends the full profile to LAN viewers, including `source.url` and `evidence.hardware[].record`, which can be local paths. | Send a display subset (id, version, register names, units, ranges) instead of the whole profile. |
| low | `lan/serve.rs`, `lan/limits.rs` | The 32-connection cap is shared before authentication. A LAN host that holds 32 idle TLS or HTTP connections can starve viewers. The limits clear after the 5 s handshake and 10 s header timeouts, but the attacker can repeat. The effect is dashboard availability only. | Add a small per-IP connection cap, and count unauthenticated connections separately. |
| low | `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, `routes.rs::csp` | `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` is allowed in both the app CSP and the LAN CSP. `script-src 'self'` holds, so the practical risk is small. | Move inline styles to classes or nonces when convenient. |
| low | `src-tauri/src/control.rs` (`control_confirm`, `control_execute`) | Confirmation is only a preview-ID match over IPC. Any script running in the webview could call arm, preview, confirm and execute in sequence. The mitigations are the strict CSP, `textContent` rendering (`dom.ts`: no `innerHTML`), and the lack of remote content. Without those, this would be a bypass. | Optional hardening: require a native confirm dialog for `risk=high` writes. Keep the "no `innerHTML`" test as a gate. |
| low | `src-tauri/src/share.rs` (`secret_store`) | On Android, MQTT passwords use `MemorySecretStore`, so they are lost on restart. This is safe, but it breaks the "Android Keystore" claim in the rules. | Keep the UI notice (`secret_persistent`) and the docs honest. Wire the Keystore before claiming parity. |
| info | `src-tauri/Cargo.toml` (`e2e` feature) | The e2e feature adds loopback sharing and writes exports to `$BUSLINK_E2E_EXPORT_DIR`. It is off by default. | Add a release-pipeline check that fails if `--features e2e` is used. |
| info | `crates/buslink-core/src/mqtt/service.rs` | The status topic is published retained (a last-will plus a status message). This is not a command, so it is allowed. The service never subscribes, so there is no inbound command path. | None. |

## Verdict per category

1. **Write frames outside `command/` and the simulator: no findings.** FC05/06/15/16 constants and encoding exist only in `command/wire.rs`. The only other users of `WriteRequest` are the simulator (decoding) and `command/mod.rs`. Tauri IPC carries only device, command and register IDs plus engineering values (`PanelRequest` uses `deny_unknown_fields`). There is no raw-PDU endpoint and no write method on `LanSource`.
2. **Command service bypass: no findings.**
   - `execute` requires the `Confirmed` state, and `ensure_armed` re-checks expiry at preview, confirm and execute.
   - `PreparedFrame` is not `Clone` and is consumed by `send`.
   - A second `execute` fails with `WrongState`.
   - Unit 0 gives `BroadcastRejected`, and the unit is range-checked against the link.
   - If the audit write fails, nothing is sent (fail-closed). Link loss disarms.
   - No retry exists anywhere in the module.
   - Reconnect, profile change and disconnect all disarm.
   - The exception is the self-asserted role above.
3. **Bounds: no findings.**
   - `check_bounds` rejects, never clamps.
   - It handles `allowed_values`, `min`/`max`, `step` and `valid_range`, rejects non-finite values, and refuses writes when no bounds exist.
   - The profile validator requires `step > 0`, which closes the NaN pass-through I suspected.
   - Comm-config values are checked: unit ID 1–247, and baud must be in the profile's code table.
   - Comm registers cannot be written outside the wizard.
4. **LAN server: no findings beyond the low items above.**
   - The guard middleware wraps every route and the fallback.
   - Order is rate limit, token, body rejection, GET-only.
   - The token is 128 bits from the OS random source, compared with `ct_eq`.
   - Bind is private IPv4 only (`check_bind` refuses `0.0.0.0`, IPv6, public and multicast), the port is ≥1024, and the server is off by default.
   - Each start gets a fresh rcgen certificate and token. Stop drops the token and key and joins the tasks.
   - There are limits on rate, failures with lockout, connections, WebSocket clients, message size and handshake time.
   - I found no logging of the token. The cookie is `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`. The WebSocket origin is checked, there is no CORS, and path traversal is blocked.
5. **MQTT: no findings.**
   - The config has no password field and rejects unknown keys.
   - The password lives in Windows Credential Manager (memory-only elsewhere), and errors go through `redact`.
   - TLS is the default. Plain `mqtt://` needs an explicit `allow_insecure`. Credentials in the URL are refused.
   - Verification uses native roots (or the platform verifier on Android) plus an optional user CA.
   - A search of non-test code found no verifier bypass. The only `dangerous()` use is a pinning client in test code.
   - There are no subscriptions.
   - The outbox is capped at 100–1M rows and holds telemetry only.
6. **Profiles, imports, exports: no findings, with limits on what I checked.** Profile JSON has a 1 MB cap, duplicate-key rejection, `deny_unknown_fields`, and no expression evaluation. `guard_text` escapes `= + - @`, tab and CR, and is used in CSV and XLSX (strings are written with `write_string`). Quality and exception columns are present in every export. I did not find the `.mbmap` or CSV import code, so I could not check its size limits.
7. **Android: no findings, partly verified.**
   - **Verified:**
     - The service is `exported="false"` with type `connectedDevice`.
     - The permission set matches the rules (no storage permissions).

**Scope.** The diff is 477 files and about 127k lines, so I did not read all of it. I read the command service, `src-tauri` IPC, the LAN and MQTT modules, Tauri config and capabilities, the Android manifests and plugin, and the export and profile guards. IEC 62443 IAC/UC is not met, and the audit identity is self-asserted. | Derive the role from a host-side setting (for example a commissioner unlock that needs a deliberate action) and not from IPC. | medium | `src-tauri/src/commands.rs` (`host_of`) and `crates/buslink-core/src/device.rs:69` | `connect_link` accepts any host name or IP for TCP. A host name such as `localhost` is fine, but a loopback IP literal makes `is_loopback_tcp()` true, and `simulated_only` profiles then count as simulator links. A port-forward or serial bridge on `127.0.0.1` pointing at real hardware would let "simulated" control commands reach a real VFD. | low | `crates/buslink-core/src/lan/routes.rs` (`authenticate`) | The token is accepted as `?t=` on every route and WebSocket, not only on `/`. <content>
---
inclusion: always
---

# Safety rules (non-negotiable)

BusLink can write to field devices. These rules apply to all code, profiles, docs and demos. When a rule and a feature request conflict, keep the rule and tell the user.

## Writes

1. **Read-only by default.** A new session, a reconnect, an app restart and a profile import all start in Monitoring. Nothing is ever written as a side effect of connecting, polling, scanning or discovery.
2. **One write path: the command service** in `crates/buslink-core/src/command/`. Only that module (and the simulator `crates/buslink-sim/`, and tests) may build FC05/06/15/16 (or FC22/23) frames or call write APIs. UI, Tauri commands, the LAN server, MQTT and the poll engine submit a command request; they never encode a write. The `guard-write-paths` hook enforces this. Name the entry point `submit`/`execute`, not `write_register`.
3. Every command passes, in order:
   - **Role and arming**: the operator arms control for one device; arming expires (default 60 s idle) and is dropped on disconnect, reconnect, profile change or app background.
   - **Bounds**: the target register must be `read_write` in the profile; the value must satisfy `min`/`max`/`step`/`allowed_values`. Out-of-bounds values are rejected, never clamped.
   - **Explicit confirmation** showing device, unit ID, register (doc address and PDU offset), old value, new value in engineering units, raw value and the encoded frame. Button labels name the action ("Apply setpoint 40 °C").
   - **Read-back verification** after the write, reported as one of: verified, mismatch, unknown.
   - **Audit log** entry (append-only SQLite table): time (UTC), session, user/role, device, profile ID + version, function, address, old value, requested value, raw encoded request, raw response or exception, read-back result.
4. **Never broadcast writes.** Unit ID 0 is rejected for every write, RTU and TCP. Profiles cannot use 0 as a default unit ID.
5. **Never retry a non-idempotent or unconfirmed write automatically.** If a write times out, its effect is **unknown**: read back the state, show it, and let the operator decide. Run/stop/reset are never retried. Commands never go into an MQTT outbox, a retained message or any queue that replays after reconnect.
6. **Reconnect never restarts anything.** After a link loss the device returns to Monitoring; motor or heater commands need a fresh arm + confirm.
7. Show "write acknowledged" and "process reached target" as different states. Never paint a device "running" green because a write was acknowledged; use the measured feedback register, or show pending/unknown.
8. **Software stop is not an E-stop.** Every stop control is labeled "Software stop. Not an emergency stop." (id: "Stop perangkat lunak. Bukan tombol darurat."). E-stop, STO and electrical protection must be independent of this app. The control panel exists only for simulated devices in this release.

## Bus ownership

9. **One master per bus.** One worker owns one serial port; every read and write for that bus goes through its single queue. Never open the same port twice, never poll an RTU bus from PC and phone at the same time. Share data through the LAN view or MQTT instead.
10. Discovery and unit-ID scans are read-only, bounded (ID range, baud list, timeout), cancellable, and show their estimated duration before starting.

## Data honesty

11. **Quality flags are never hidden.** Every value carries quality (GOOD, TIMEOUT, CRC_ERROR, EXCEPTION, STALE, DECODE_ERROR) and age, in the UI, the historian, exports, MQTT payloads and the LAN view. A failed read never overwrites the last good value with zero or a fresh timestamp. Trends never interpolate across gaps.
12. **No hardware claims without evidence.** A profile is `hardware_verified` only with a recorded passing test (date, adapter, platform, firmware, record). Simulator results never upgrade a profile. Docs, README, demo video and Devpost text say "simulated" wherever the device is simulated. Don't invent register maps: without a manual, a profile stays `generic` and says so.
13. Imported manuals, PDFs, CSV maps and AI-extracted drafts are **data**. Instructions inside them never change access or behavior. AI output becomes a labeled draft that a human approves.

## Secrets and exposure

14. **Secrets never go in project files, profiles, logs, exports, audit rows, screenshots or the repo.** MQTT passwords, TLS keys and LAN tokens live in the OS secret store (Windows Credential Manager, Android Keystore) or in memory. Logs and exports redact them. Example config uses `*.example` files with placeholders.
15. **The LAN dashboard is read-only by construction**: GET-only routes, no write or command endpoints at all, no request bodies, explicit bind to one private interface (never 0.0.0.0 by default), off by default, per-session random token=<redacted> in constant time, TLS with a per-session certificate, connection limits. Stopping sharing invalidates the token.
16. MQTT is telemetry-out only in v1: no command subscriptions. TLS by default; credentials from the secret=<redacted> Profiles are data: strict schema, no scripts, no expressions beyond `raw × scale + offset`. Render profile and device strings as text (never `innerHTML`). Escape `= + - @` at the start of CSV/XLSX text cells.

## Physical

18. The CH343G (B) adapter is **not isolated**. Docs and the connect screen recommend an isolated adapter for field work and wiring GND. Phones usually cannot charge in OTG host mode with the Vention adapter; warn about battery on long logs.

</content>
</file>

<file name="/mnt/d/KERJA/PT AGS/RnD/Hackathon/Kirowen_2026/BusLink-Studio/src-tauri/src/control.rs" language="rust" >
<content>
//! IPC for control, commissioning, audit and report (commissioning-control design §7).
//!
//! Requests carry device IDs, command IDs, register IDs and engineering values
//! only: no frame, address or function code ever comes from the webview. All
//! checks (arming, bounds, confirmation, single send, read-back, audit) happen
//! in `buslink_core::command`. Calls that may wait for the link worker run off
//! the main thread.

use crate::state::AppState;
use buslink_core::command::commission::Wizard;
use buslink_core::command::control::{Control, ControlStatus};
use buslink_core::command::{CommSettingKind, CommandOutcome, CommandRequest, DisarmReason, Preview, Role};
use buslink_core::export::report::ReportData;
use buslink_core::historian::AuditRow;
use buslink_core::session::{ExportFormat, Session};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::sync::Arc;
use tauri::{AppHandle, State};

type R<T> = Result<T, String>;

const MAX_REPORT_BYTES: usize = 5 * 1024 * 1024;

async fn blocking<T: Send + 'static>(
    control: Arc<Control>,
    f: impl FnOnce(&Control) -> R<T> + Send + 'static,
) -> R<T> {
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || f(&control))
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case", deny_unknown_fields)]
pub enum PanelRequest {
    /// A profile command (run, stop, setpoint, ...).
    Named { command: String, value: Option<f64> },
    /// A `read_write` register by profile ID, in engineering units.
    Register { register: String, value: f64 },
}

impl From<PanelRequest> for CommandRequest {
    fn from(r: PanelRequest) -> Self {
        match r {
            PanelRequest::Named { command, value } => CommandRequest::Named { command, value },
            PanelRequest::Register { register, value } => CommandRequest::SetRegister { register, value },
        }
    }
}

#[tauri::command]
pub async fn control_status(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> R<ControlStatus> {
    blocking(Arc::clone(&state.control), |c| Ok(c.status())).await
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct ArmReq {
    device_id: String,
    user: String,
    role: Role,
}

#[tauri::command]
pub async fn control_arm(state: State<'_, AppState>, req: ArmReq) -> R<ControlStatus> {
    if req.role == Role::Viewer {
        return Err("a viewer cannot arm control".into());
    }
    blocking(Arc::clone(&state.control), move |c| {
        c.arm(&req.device_id, &req.user, req.role).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
    })
    .await
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum DisarmWhy {
    Operator,
    AppBackground,
}

#[tauri::command]
pub async fn control_disarm(state: State<'_, AppState>, reason: DisarmWhy) -> R<ControlStatus> {
    let reason = match reason {
        DisarmWhy::Operator => DisarmReason::Operator,
        DisarmWhy::AppBackground => DisarmReason::AppBackground,
    };
    blocking(Arc::clone(&state.control), move |c| Ok(c.disarm(reason))).await

//! Links (one bus or connection each) and device instances. A device
//! instance holds site settings and points at a profile by ID and version;
//! one profile serves many instances.

use crate::profile::Profile;
use crate::protocol::pdu::{MAX_READ_BITS, MAX_READ_REGISTERS};
use crate::protocol::rtu::{RtuTiming, SerialSettings};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::net::IpAddr;
use thiserror::Error;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum LinkKind {
    /// Serial RTU. `port` is the OS port (COM3, /dev/ttyUSB0) or the Android `<deviceName>#<index>`.
    Rtu { port: String, serial: SerialSettings },
    /// Modbus TCP (MBAP).
    Tcp { host: String, port: u16 },
    /// Raw RTU frames (with CRC) through a transparent serial server. Not MBAP.
    RtuOverTcp {
        host: String,
        port: u16,
        serial: SerialSettings,
    },
    /// In-process simulator bus.
    Simulator { name: String, serial: SerialSettings },
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct LinkConfig {
    pub id: String,
    pub kind: LinkKind,
    /// Floor for the inter-frame gap (Android: 50 ms).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub min_inter_frame_ms: u64,
}

impl LinkConfig {
    /// Key that identifies the physical resource: two links with the same key
    /// would be two masters on one bus.
    pub fn owner_key(&self) -> String {
        match &self.kind {
            LinkKind::Rtu { port, .. } => format!("serial:{}", port.to_ascii_lowercase()),
            LinkKind::Tcp { host, port } => format!("tcp:{}:{port}", host.to_ascii_lowercase()),
            LinkKind::RtuOverTcp { host, port, .. } => format!("rtu-tcp:{}:{port}", host.to_ascii_lowercase()),
            LinkKind::Simulator { name, .. } => format!("sim:{name}"),
        }
    }

    /// True when responses are RTU frames (serial, RTU-over-TCP, simulator bus).
    pub fn uses_rtu_framing(&self) -> bool {
        !matches!(self.kind, LinkKind::Tcp { .. })
    }

    pub fn serial(&self) -> Option<SerialSettings> {
        match &self.kind {
            LinkKind::Rtu { serial, .. } | LinkKind::RtuOverTcp { serial, .. } | LinkKind::Simulator { serial, .. } => {
                Some(*serial)
            }
            LinkKind::Tcp { .. } => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn is_simulator(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.kind, LinkKind::Simulator { .. })
    }

    /// A TCP link whose host is a loopback IP literal (the training TCP server).
    pub fn is_loopback_tcp(&self) -> bool {
        match &self.kind {
            LinkKind::Tcp { host, .. } => host.parse::<IpAddr>().is_ok_and(|ip| ip.is_loopback()),
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    /// Maximum unit ID allowed for this link (247 on serial lines, 255 on TCP).
    pub fn max_unit_id(&self) -> u8 {
        if self.uses_rtu_framing() { 247 } else { 255 }
    }

    pub fn inter_frame_ms(&self) -> u64 {
        match self.serial() {
            Some(s) => RtuTiming::new(&s).inter_frame_ms(self.min_inter_frame_ms),
            None => self.min_inter_frame_ms,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DeviceInstance {
    pub id: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub link_id: String,
    pub unit_id: u8,
    pub profile_id: String,
    pub profile_version: String,
    pub poll_interval_ms: u64,
    /// Default `max(3 × poll interval, 3 s)`.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub stale_after_ms: Option<u64>,
    /// Default: profile, else derived from the serial settings.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub response_timeout_ms: Option<u64>,
    /// Read retries on timeout/CRC error (writes are never retried).
    #[serde(default = "default_retries")]
    pub read_retries: u8,
    /// Unused addresses a merged read may span. 0 = contiguous only.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub max_gap: u16,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub max_registers_per_read: Option<u16>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub max_bits_per_read: Option<u16>,
}

fn default_retries() -> u8 {
    1
}

pub const MIN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS: u64 = 100;
pub const MAX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS: u64 = 86_400_000;

#[derive(Debug, Error, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DeviceError {
    #[error("unit ID 0 is broadcast and cannot be a device")]
    UnitZero,
    #[error("unit ID {unit} is above {max} for this link")]
    UnitRange { unit: u8, max: u8 },
    #[error("device uses profile {expected}, got {got}")]
    ProfileMismatch { expected: String, got: String },
    #[error("device is on link '{expected}', got '{got}'")]
    LinkMismatch { expected: String, got: String },
    #[error("poll interval {0} ms outside {MIN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS}..={MAX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS}")]
    PollInterval(u64),
    #[error("read limit {0} outside the spec range")]
    ReadLimit(u16),
    #[error("read retries {0} above 3")]
    Retries(u8),
    #[error("device id must be 1-64 characters of a-z, 0-9, '-', '_' or '.'")]
    Id,
}

impl DeviceInstance {
    /// A device using the profile's defaults for the given link kind.
    pub fn from_profile(id: &str, name: &str, link: &LinkConfig, profile: &Profile) -> DeviceInstance {
        let unit_id = if link.uses_rtu_framing() {
            profile
                .transport
                .rtu
                .map(|r| r.unit_id)
                .or(profile.transport.tcp.map(|t| t.unit_id))
        } else {
            profile
                .transport
                .tcp
                .map(|t| t.unit_id)
                .or(profile.transport.rtu.map(|r| r.unit_id))
        };
        DeviceInstance {
            id: id.to_owned(),
            name: name.to_owned(),
            link_id: link.id.clone(),
            unit_id: unit_id.unwrap_or(1),
            profile_id: profile.profile_id.clone(),
            profile_version: profile.profile_version.clone(),
            poll_interval_ms: 1000,
            stale_after_ms: None,
            response_timeout_ms: None,
            read_retries: default_retries(),
            max_gap: 0,
            max_registers_per_read: None,
            max_bits_per_read: None,
        }
    }

    pub fn check(&self, profile: &Profile, link: &LinkConfig) -> Result<(), DeviceError> {
        let id_ok = (1..=64).contains(&self.id.len())
            && self
                .id
                .bytes()
                .all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c.is_ascii_digit() || matches!(c, b'-' | b'_' | b'.'));
        if !id_ok {
            return Err(DeviceError::Id);
        }
        if self.unit_id == 0 {
            return Err(DeviceError::UnitZero);
        }
        if self.unit_id > link.max_unit_id() {
            return Err(DeviceError::UnitRange {
                unit: self.unit_id,
                max: link.max_unit_id(),
            });
        }
        if self.profile_id != profile.profile_id || self.profile_version != profile.profile_version {
            return Err(DeviceError::ProfileMismatch {
                expected: format!("{}@{}", self.profile_id, self.profile_version),
                got: profile.key(),
            });
        }
        if self.link_id != link.id {
            return Err(DeviceError::LinkMismatch {
                expected: self.link_id.clone(),
                got: link.id.clone(),
            });
        }
        if !(MIN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS..=MAX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS).contains(&self.poll_interval_ms) {
            return Err(DeviceError::PollInterval(self.poll_interval_ms));
        }
        if let Some(n) = self.max_registers_per_read
            && !(1..=MAX_READ_REGISTERS).contains(&n)
        {
            return Err(DeviceError::ReadLimit(n));
        }
        if let Some(n) = self.max_bits_per_read
            && !(1..=MAX_READ_BITS).contains(&n)
        {
            return Err(DeviceError::ReadLimit(n));
        }
        if self.read_retries > 3 {
            return Err(DeviceError::Retries(self.read_retries));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn stale_threshold_ms(&self) -> u64 {
        self.stale_after_ms
            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.poll_interval_ms.saturating_mul(3).max(3000))
    }

    /// Instance setting, else profile default for the link kind, else derived from the serial settings.
    pub fn timeout_ms(&self, profile: &Profile, link: &LinkConfig) -> u64 {
        if let Some(t) = self.response_timeout_ms {
            return t;
        }
        let from_profile = if link.uses_rtu_framing() {
            profile.transport.rtu.and_then(|r| r.response_timeout_ms)
        } else {
            profile.transport.tcp.and_then(|t| t.response_timeout_ms)
        };
        if let Some(t) = from_profile {
            return u64::from(t);
        }
        match link.serial() {
            Some(s) => RtuTiming::new(&s).default_response_timeout_ms(),
            None => 1000,
        }
    }
}

//! Links (one bus or connection each) and device instances. A device
//! instance holds site settings and points at a profile by ID and version;
//! one profile serves many instances.

use crate::profile::Profile;
use crate::protocol::pdu::{MAX_READ_BITS, MAX_READ_REGISTERS};
use crate::protocol::rtu::{RtuTiming, SerialSettings};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::net::IpAddr;
use thiserror::Error;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum LinkKind {
    /// Serial RTU. `port` is the OS port (COM3, /dev/ttyUSB0) or the Android `<deviceName>#<index>`.
    Rtu { port: String, serial: SerialSettings },
    /// Modbus TCP (MBAP).
    Tcp { host: String, port: u16 },
    /// Raw RTU frames (with CRC) through a transparent serial server. Not MBAP.
    RtuOverTcp {
        host: String,
        port: u16,
        serial: SerialSettings,
    },
    /// In-process simulator bus.
    Simulator { name: String, serial: SerialSettings },
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct LinkConfig {
    pub id: String,
    pub kind: LinkKind,
    /// Floor for the inter-frame gap (Android: 50 ms).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub min_inter_frame_ms: u64,
}

impl LinkConfig {
    /// Key that identifies the physical resource: two links with the same key
    /// would be two masters on one bus.
    pub fn owner_key(&self) -> String {
        match &self.kind {
            LinkKind::Rtu { port, .. } => format!("serial:{}", port.to_ascii_lowercase()),
            LinkKind::Tcp { host, port } => format!("tcp:{}:{port}", host.to_ascii_lowercase()),
            LinkKind::RtuOverTcp { host, port, .. } => format!("rtu-tcp:{}:{port}", host.to_ascii_lowercase()),
            LinkKind::Simulator { name, .. } => format!("sim:{name}"),
        }
    }

    /// True when responses are RTU frames (serial, RTU-over-TCP, simulator bus).
    pub fn uses_rtu_framing(&self) -> bool {
        !matches!(self.kind, LinkKind::Tcp { .. })
    }

    pub fn serial(&self) -> Option<SerialSettings> {
        match &self.kind {
            LinkKind::Rtu { serial, .. } | LinkKind::RtuOverTcp { serial, .. } | LinkKind::Simulator { serial, .. } => {
                Some(*serial)
            }
            LinkKind::Tcp { .. } => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn is_simulator(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.kind, LinkKind::Simulator { .. })
    }

    /// A TCP link whose host is a loopback IP literal (the training TCP server).
    pub fn is_loopback_tcp(&self) -> bool {
        match &self.kind {
            LinkKind::Tcp { host, .. } => host.parse::<IpAddr>().is_ok_and(|ip| ip.is_loopback()),
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    /// Maximum unit ID allowed for this link (247 on serial lines, 255 on TCP).
    pub fn max_unit_id(&self) -> u8 {
        if self.uses_rtu_framing() { 247 } else { 255 }
    }

    pub fn inter_frame_ms(&self) -> u64 {
        match self.serial() {
            Some(s) => RtuTiming::new(&s).inter_frame_ms(self.min_inter_frame_ms),
            None => self.min_inter_frame_ms,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DeviceInstance {
    pub id: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub link_id: String,
    pub unit_id: u8,
    pub profile_id: String,
    pub profile_version: String,
    pub poll_interval_ms: u64,
    /// Default `max(3 × poll interval, 3 s)`.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub stale_after_ms: Option<u64>,
    /// Default: profile, else derived from the serial settings.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub response_timeout_ms: Option<u64>,
    /// Read retries on timeout/CRC error (writes are never retried).
    #[serde(default = "default_retries")]
    pub read_retries: u8,
    /// Unused addresses a merged read may span. 0 = contiguous only.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub max_gap: u16,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub max_registers_per_read: Option<u16>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub max_bits_per_read: Option<u16>,
}

fn default_retries() -> u8 {
    1
}

pub const MIN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS: u64 = 100;
pub const MAX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS: u64 = 86_400_000;

#[derive(Debug, Error, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DeviceError {
    #[error("unit ID 0 is broadcast and cannot be a device")]
    UnitZero,
    #[error("unit ID {unit} is above {max} for this link")]
    UnitRange { unit: u8, max: u8 },
    #[error("device uses profile {expected}, got {got}")]
    ProfileMismatch { expected: String, got: String },
    #[error("device is on link '{expected}', got '{got}'")]
    LinkMismatch { expected: String, got: String },
    #[error("poll interval {0} ms outside {MIN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS}..={MAX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS}")]
    PollInterval(u64),
    #[error("read limit {0} outside the spec range")]
    ReadLimit(u16),
    #[error("read retries {0} above 3")]
    Retries(u8),
    #[error("device id must be 1-64 characters of a-z, 0-9, '-', '_' or '.'")]
    Id,
}

impl DeviceInstance {
    /// A device using the profile's defaults for the given link kind.
    pub fn from_profile(id: &str, name: &str, link: &LinkConfig, profile: &Profile) -> DeviceInstance {
        let unit_id = if link.uses_rtu_framing() {
            profile
                .transport
                .rtu
                .map(|r| r.unit_id)
                .or(profile.transport.tcp.map(|t| t.unit_id))
        } else {
            profile
                .transport
                .tcp
                .map(|t| t.unit_id)
                .or(profile.transport.rtu.map(|r| r.unit_id))
        };
        DeviceInstance {
            id: id.to_owned(),
            name: name.to_owned(),
            link_id: link.id.clone(),
            unit_id: unit_id.unwrap_or(1),
            profile_id: profile.profile_id.clone(),
            profile_version: profile.profile_version.clone(),
            poll_interval_ms: 1000,
            stale_after_ms: None,
            response_timeout_ms: None,
            read_retries: default_retries(),
            max_gap: 0,
            max_registers_per_read: None,
            max_bits_per_read: None,
        }
    }

    pub fn check(&self, profile: &Profile, link: &LinkConfig) -> Result<(), DeviceError> {
        let id_ok = (1..=64).contains(&self.id.len())
            && self
                .id
                .bytes()
                .all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c.is_ascii_digit() || matches!(c, b'-' | b'_' | b'.'));
        if !id_ok {
            return Err(DeviceError::Id);
        }
        if self.unit_id == 0 {
            return Err(DeviceError::UnitZero);
        }
        if self.unit_id > link.max_unit_id() {
            return Err(DeviceError::UnitRange {
                unit: self.unit_id,
                max: link.max_unit_id(),
            });
        }
        if self.profile_id != profile.profile_id || self.profile_version != profile.profile_version {
            return Err(DeviceError::ProfileMismatch {
                expected: format!("{}@{}", self.profile_id, self.profile_version),
                got: profile.key(),
            });
        }
        if self.link_id != link.id {
            return Err(DeviceError::LinkMismatch {
                expected: self.link_id.clone(),
                got: link.id.clone(),
            });
        }
        if !(MIN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS..=MAX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS).contains(&self.poll_interval_ms) {
            return Err(DeviceError::PollInterval(self.poll_interval_ms));
        }
        if let Some(n) = self.max_registers_per_read
            && !(1..=MAX_READ_REGISTERS).contains(&n)
        {
            return Err(DeviceError::ReadLimit(n));
        }
        if let Some(n) = self.max_bits_per_read
            && !(1..=MAX_READ_BITS).contains(&n)
        {
            return Err(DeviceError::ReadLimit(n));
        }
        if self.read_retries > 3 {
            return Err(DeviceError::Retries(self.read_retries));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn stale_threshold_ms(&self) -> u64 {
        self.stale_after_ms
            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.poll_interval_ms.saturating_mul(3).max(3000))
    }

    /// Instance setting, else profile default for the link kind, else derived from the serial settings.
    pub fn timeout_ms(&self, profile: &Profile, link: &LinkConfig) -> u64 {
        if let Some(t) = self.response_timeout_ms {
            return t;
        }
        let from_profile = if link.uses_rtu_framing() {
            profile.transport.rtu.and_then(|r| r.response_timeout_ms)
        } else {
            profile.transport.tcp.and_then(|t| t.response_timeout_ms)
        };
        if let Some(t) = from_profile {
            return u64::from(t);
        }
        match link.serial() {
            Some(s) => RtuTiming::new(&s).default_response_timeout_ms(),
            None => 1000,
        }
    }
}

//! IPC commands (app-shell-desktop design §9). Monitoring only: no command here
//! encodes or submits a write; control requests live in `control.rs` and go to
//! the command service. No command accepts a file path or a raw frame.

use crate::serial::{self, PortView};
use crate::state::{AppState, platform};
use buslink_core::alarm::{AlarmDef, AlarmSnapshot, default_deadband, default_delay_ms};
use buslink_core::device::{DeviceInstance, LinkConfig, LinkKind};
use buslink_core::historian::{EventRow, SessionInfo};
use buslink_core::profile::Profile;
use buslink_core::protocol::rtu::{Parity, SerialSettings};
use buslink_core::session::{DeviceInspection, ExportFormat, LiveSnapshot, Session, SessionError};
use buslink_core::trend::TrendSeries;
use buslink_sim::training::{ActiveFault, TRAINING_DEVICES, TRAINING_LINK_ID, Training, TrainingFault, alarm_presets};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::sync::Arc;
use tauri::{AppHandle, State};

type R<T> = Result<T, String>;

fn err(e: SessionError) -> String {
    e.to_string()
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct AppInfo {
    name: &'static str,
    version: &'static str,
    platform: &'static str,
    session_id: String,
    historian_path: Option<String>,
    profile_errors: Vec<String>,
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn app_info(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> AppInfo {
    AppInfo {
        name: "BusLink Studio",
        version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
        platform: platform(),
        session_id: state.session.session_id().to_owned(),
        historian_path: state.db_path.as_ref().map(|p| p.display().to_string()),
        profile_errors: state.profile_errors.clone(),
    }
}

#[tauri::command]
pub async fn list_ports(app: AppHandle) -> R<Vec<PortView>> {
    // Android port listing calls into Kotlin and blocks: keep it off the main thread.
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || serial::list(&app))
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct ProfileView {
    key: String,
    profile: Profile,
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn list_profiles(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> Vec<ProfileView> {
    state
        .session
        .profiles()
        .iter()
        .map(|p| ProfileView {
            key: p.key(),
            profile: (**p).clone(),
        })
        .collect()
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct ConnectReq {
    /// `rtu`, `tcp` or `rtu_over_tcp`
    kind: String,
    port: Option<String>,
    baud: Option<u32>,
    data_bits: Option<u8>,
    parity: Option<Parity>,
    stop_bits: Option<u8>,
    host: Option<String>,
    tcp_port: Option<u16>,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct ConnectResult {
    link_id: String,
    /// RTU links show the non-isolated adapter advice (safety rule 18).
    isolation_advice: bool,
    /// Android RTU over OTG: the phone usually cannot charge, mind the battery (safety rule 18).
    otg_battery_advice: bool,
    /// Android: baud above 115 200 can lose fragments (research/03 row 37).
    high_baud_warning: bool,
}

/// What Start polling achieved beyond polling itself (android-otg Req 6.7).
#[derive(Serialize, Default)]
pub struct StartResult {
    android: bool,
    /// The foreground service runs, so polling continues with the screen off.
    background: bool,
    notifications_denied: bool,
    error: Option<String>,
}

fn slug(s: &str) -> String {
    let out: String = s
        .chars()
        .map(|c| {
            if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
                c.to_ascii_lowercase()
            } else {
                '-'
            }
        })
        .collect();
    out.trim_matches('-').chars().take(40).collect()
}

fn serial_of(r: &ConnectReq) -> R<SerialSettings> {
    let s = SerialSettings::new(
        r.baud.unwrap_or(9600),
        r.data_bits.unwrap_or(8),
        r.parity.unwrap_or(Parity::None),
        r.stop_bits.unwrap_or(1),
    );
    s.validate().map_err(str::to_owned)?;
    Ok(s)
}

fn host_of(r: &ConnectReq) -> R<(String, u16)> {
    let host = r.host.as_deref().map(str::trim).unwrap_or_default();
    let ok = !host.is_empty()
        && host.len() <= 253
        && host
            .chars()
            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '.' | '-' | ':' | '[' | ']'));
    if !ok {
        return Err("host must be an IP address or host name".into());
    }
    let port = r.tcp_port.unwrap_or(502);
    if port == 0 {
        return Err("TCP port must be 1-65535".into());
    }
    Ok((host.to_owned(), port))
}

#[tauri::command]
pub async fn connect_link(state: State<'_, AppState>, req: ConnectReq) -> R<ConnectResult> {
    // Opening a USB port may show the Android permission dialog and wait for the
    // answer, which arrives on the main thread: run off it.
    let session = Arc::clone(&state.session);
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || connect_blocking(&session, req))
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
}

fn connect_blocking(session: &Session, req: ConnectReq) -> R<ConnectResult> {
    let android = cfg!(target_os = "android");
    let mut high_baud_warning = false;
    let (config, rtu) = match req.kind.as_str() {
        "rtu" => {
            let port = req.port.clone().unwrap_or_default();
            if port.trim().is_empty() || port.len() > 64 {
                return Err("choose a serial port".into());
            }
            let serial = serial_of(&req)?;
            high_baud_warning = android && serial.baud > crate::android_usb::MAX_RELIABLE_BAUD;
            (
                LinkConfig {
                    id: slug(&port),
                    kind: LinkKind::Rtu { port, serial },
                    // Android USB-serial needs at least 50 ms between frames (modbus.md).
                    min_inter_frame_ms: if android { 50 } else { 0 },
                },
                true,
            )
        }
        "tcp" => {
            let (host, port) = host_of(&req)?;
            (
                LinkConfig {
                    id: format!("tcp-{}-{port}", slug(&host)),
                    kind: LinkKind::Tcp { host, port },
                    min_inter_frame_ms: 0,
                },
                false,
            )
        }
        "rtu_over_tcp" => {
            let (host, port) = host_of(&req)?;
            let serial = serial_of(&req)?;
            (
                LinkConfig {
                    id: format!("rtutcp-{}-{port}", slug(&host)),
                    kind: LinkKind::RtuOverTcp { host, port, serial },
                    min_inter_frame_ms: 0,
                },
                false,
            )
        }
        _ => return Err("unknown link kind".into()),
    };
    let link_id = config.id.clone();
    session.connect(config, false).map_err(err)?;
    Ok(ConnectResult {
        link_id,
        isolation_advice: rtu,
        otg_battery_advice: android && rtu,
        high_baud_warning,
    })
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn reconnect_link(state: State<'_, AppState>, id: String) -> R<()> {
    state.session.reconnect(&id).map_err(err)
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn disconnect_link(state: State<'_, AppState>, id: String) -> R<()> {
    state.session.disconnect(&id).map_err(err)
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn remove_link(state: State<'_, AppState>, id: String) -> R<()> {
    state.session.remove_link(&id).map_err(err)
}

#[tauri::command]
pub async fn start_polling(app: AppHandle, state: State<'_, AppState>, id: String) -> R<StartResult> {
    let session = Arc::clone(&state.session);
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || -> R<StartResult> {
        #[cfg(target_os = "android")]
        {
            // Foreground service first (user action, app in foreground, USB permission already
            // held because the port is open). A failure is reported; polling still starts.
            let link = session.link_status().into_iter().find(|l| l.id == id);
            let bg = match link {
                Some(l) if !l.simulated => {
                    let devices = u32::try_from(l.devices.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
                    Some(crate::android_usb::start_service(&app, &l.label, devices))
                }
                _ => None,
            };
            if let Err(e) = session.start_polling(&id) {
                if bg.as_ref().is_some_and(|b| b.background) {
                    crate::android_usb::stop_service(&app);
                }
                return Err(err(e));
            }
            let bg = bg.unwrap_or_default();
            Ok(StartResult {
                android: true,
                background: bg.background,
                notifications_denied: bg.notifications_denied,
                error: bg.error,
            })
        }
        #[cfg(not(target_os = "android"))]
        {
            let _ = &app;
            session.start_polling(&id).map_err(err)?;
            Ok(StartResult::default())
        }
    })
    .await
    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn stop_polling(state: State<'_, AppState>, id: String) -> R<()> {
    state.session.stop_polling(&id).map_err(err)
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct AddDeviceReq {
    link_id: String,
    profile_key: String,
    unit_id: u8,
    name: Option<String>,
    poll_interval_ms: Option<u64>,
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn add_device(state: State<'_, AppState>, req: AddDeviceReq) -> R<String> {
    let s = &state.session;

            units: t.world().lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).units(),
            faults: t.active(),

            link_id: TRAINING_LINK_ID,

            faults: Vec::new(),

/// Start Training mode: a simulated bus with three devices, alarm presets, polling on.
#[tauri::command]
pub fn training_start(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> R<TrainingStatus> {
    let s = &state.session;
    {
        let mut t = state.training.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        if t.is_none() {
            let seed = u64::try_from(state.clock.utc_ms()).unwrap_or(1);
            *t = Some(Arc::new(Training::new(seed, Arc::clone(&state.clock))));
        }
    }
    let existing = s.links().into_iter().find(|l| l.id == TRAINING_LINK_ID);
    match existing {
        Some(l) if l.state == buslink_core::session::LinkState::Polling => {}
        Some(l) => {
            if matches!(
                l.state,
                buslink_core::session::LinkState::Disconnected | buslink_core::session::LinkState::Down
            ) {
                s.reconnect(TRAINING_LINK_ID).map_err(err)?;
            }
            s.start_polling(TRAINING_LINK_ID).map_err(err)?;
        }
        None => {
            let link = Training::link_config();
            s.connect(link.clone(), true).map_err(err)?;
            let mut ids = Vec::new();
            for (unit, profile_id) in TRAINING_DEVICES {
                let Some(p) = s.profiles().into_iter().find(|p| p.profile_id == profile_id) else {
                    return Err(format!("bundled profile {profile_id} missing"));
                };
                let id = s.suggest_device_id(&p.profile_id, unit);
                let mut d = DeviceInstance::from_profile(&id, &format!("{} (simulated)", p.model.get("en")), &link, &p);
                d.unit_id = unit;
                d.response_timeout_ms = Some(300);
                s.add_device(d).map_err(err)?;
                ids.push(id);
            }
            if let [soil, vfd, temp] = ids.as_slice() {
                for a in alarm_presets(soil, vfd, temp) {
                    s.alarm_add(a).map_err(err)?;
                }
            }
            s.start_polling(TRAINING_LINK_ID).map_err(err)?;
        }
    }
    Ok(training_status(state))
}

fn slug(s: &str) -> String {
    let out: String = s
        .chars()
        .map(|c| {
            if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
                c.to_ascii_lowercase()
            } else {
                '-'
            }
        })
        .collect();
    out.trim_matches('-').chars().take(40).collect()
}

fn serial_of(r: &ConnectReq) -> R<SerialSettings> {
    let s = SerialSettings::new(
        r.baud.unwrap_or(9600),
        r.data_bits.unwrap_or(8),
        r.parity.unwrap_or(Parity::None),
        r.stop_bits.unwrap_or(1),
    );
    s.validate().map_err(str::to_owned)?;
    Ok(s)
}

fn host_of(r: &ConnectReq) -> R<(String, u16)> {
    let host = r.host.as_deref().map(str::trim).unwrap_or_default();
    let ok = !host.is_empty()
        && host.len() <= 253
        && host
            .chars()
            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '.' | '-' | ':' | '[' | ']'));
    if !ok {
        return Err("host must be an IP address or host name".into());
    }
    let port = r.tcp_port.unwrap_or(502);
    if port == 0 {
        return Err("TCP port must be 1-65535".into());
    }
    Ok((host.to_owned(), port))
}

#[tauri::command]
pub async fn connect_link(state: State<'_, AppState>, req: ConnectReq) -> R<ConnectResult> {
    // Opening a USB port may show the Android permission dialog and wait for the
    // answer, which arrives on the main thread: run off it.
    let session = Arc::clone(&state.session);
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || connect_blocking(&session, req))
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
}

fn connect_blocking(session: &Session, req: ConnectReq) -> R<ConnectResult> {
    let android = cfg!(target_os = "android");
    let mut high_baud_warning = false;
    let (config, rtu) = match req.kind.as_str() {
        "rtu" => {
            let port = req.port.clone().unwrap_or_default();
            if port.trim().is_empty() || port.len() > 64 {
                return Err("choose a serial port".into());
            }
            let serial = serial_of(&req)?;
            high_baud_warning = android && serial.baud > crate::android_usb::MAX_RELIABLE_BAUD;
            (
                LinkConfig {
                    id: slug(&port),
                    kind: LinkKind::Rtu { port, serial },
                    // Android USB-serial needs at least 50 ms between frames (modbus.md).
                    min_inter_frame_ms: if android { 50 } else { 0 },
                },
                true,
            )
        }
        "tcp" => {
            let (host, port) = host_of(&req)?;
            (
                LinkConfig {
                    id: format!("tcp-{}-{port}", slug(&host)),
                    kind: LinkKind::Tcp { host, port },
                    min_inter_frame_ms: 0,
                },
                false,
            )
        }
        "rtu_over_tcp" => {
            let (host, port) = host_of(&req)?;
            let serial = serial_of(&req)?;
            (
                LinkConfig {
                    id: format!("rtutcp-{}-{port}", slug(&host)),
                    kind: LinkKind::RtuOverTcp { host, port, serial },
                    min_inter_frame_ms: 0,
                },
                false,
            )
        }
        _ => return Err("unknown link kind".into()),
    };
    let link_id = config.id.clone();
    session.connect(config, false).map_err(err)?;
    Ok(ConnectResult {
        link_id,
        isolation_advice: rtu,
        otg_battery_advice: android && rtu,
        high_baud_warning,
    })
}

    let session = Arc::clone(&state.session);
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || -> R<StartResult> {
        #[cfg(target_os = "android")]
        {
            // Foreground service first (user action, app in foreground, USB permission already
            // held because the port is open). A failure is reported; polling still starts.
            let link = session.link_status().into_iter().find(|l| l.id == id);
            let bg = match link {
                Some(l) if !l.simulated => {
                    let devices = u32::try_from(l.devices.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
                    Some(crate::android_usb::start_service(&app, &l.label, devices))
                }
                _ => None,
            };
            if let Err(e) = session.start_polling(&id) {
                if bg.as_ref().is_some_and(|b| b.background) {
                    crate::android_usb::stop_service(&app);
                }
                return Err(err(e));
            }
            let bg = bg.unwrap_or_default();
            Ok(StartResult {
                android: true,
                background: bg.background,
                notifications_denied: bg.notifications_denied,
                error: bg.error,
            })
        }
        #[cfg(not(target_os = "android"))]
        {
            let _ = &app;
            session.start_polling(&id).map_err(err)?;
            Ok(StartResult::default())
        }
    })
    .await
    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct ShelveReq {
    id: String,
    minutes: u32,
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn alarm_shelve(state: State<'_, AppState>, req: ShelveReq) -> R<()> {
    state
        .session
        .alarm_shelve(&req.id, u64::from(req.minutes) * 60_000)
        .map_err(err)
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn alarm_unshelve(state: State<'_, AppState>, id: String) -> R<()> {
    state.session.alarm_unshelve(&id).map_err(err)
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct OosReq {
    id: String,
    out_of_service: bool,
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn alarm_set_oos(state: State<'_, AppState>, req: OosReq) -> R<()> {
    state
        .session
        .alarm_set_out_of_service(&req.id, req.out_of_service)
        .map_err(err)
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn alarm_events(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> R<Vec<EventRow>> {
    state.session.events(Some("alarm"), 500).map_err(err)
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct AlarmDefaults {
    deadband: f64,
    delay_ms: u64,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct DefaultsReq {
    unit: Option<String>,
    span: f64,
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn alarm_defaults(req: DefaultsReq) -> AlarmDefaults {
    AlarmDefaults {
        deadband: default_deadband(req.unit.as_deref(), req.span),
        delay_ms: default_delay_ms(req.unit.as_deref()),
    }
}

// ---- training ----

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct TrainingStatus {
    started: bool,
    link_id: &'static str,
    units: Vec<u8>,
    faults: Vec<ActiveFault>,
}

fn training_of(state: &AppState) -> Option<Arc<Training>> {
    state.training.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone()
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn training_status(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> TrainingStatus {
    match training_of(&state) {
        Some(t) => TrainingStatus {
            started: true,
            link_id: TRAINING_LINK_ID,
            units: t.world().lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).units(),
            faults: t.active(),
        },
        None => TrainingStatus {
            started: false,
            link_id: TRAINING_LINK_ID,
            units: Vec::new(),
            faults: Vec::new(),
        },
    }
}

/// Start Training mode: a simulated bus with three devices, alarm presets, polling on.
#[tauri::command]
pub fn training_start(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> R<TrainingStatus> {
    let s = &state.session;
    {
        let mut t = state.training.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        if t.is_none() {
            let seed = u64::try_from(state.clock.utc_ms()).unwrap_or(1);
            *t = Some(Arc::new(Training::new(seed, Arc::clone(&state.clock))));
        }
    }
    let existing = s.links().into_iter().find(|l| l.id == TRAINING_LINK_ID);
    match existing {
        Some(l) if l.state == buslink_core::session::LinkState::Polling => {}
        Some(l) => {
            if matches!(
                l.state,
                buslink_core::session::LinkState::Disconnected | buslink_core::session::LinkState::Down
            ) {
                s.reconnect(TRAINING_LINK_ID).map_err(err)?;
            }
            s.start_polling(TRAINING_LINK_ID).map_err(err)?;
        }
        None => {
            let link = Training::link_config();
            s.connect(link.clone(), true).map_err(err)?;
            let mut ids = Vec::new();
            for (unit, profile_id) in TRAINING_DEVICES {
                let Some(p) = s.profiles().into_iter().find(|p| p.profile_id == profile_id) else {
                    return Err(format!("bundled profile {profile_id} missing"));
                };
                let id = s.suggest_device_id(&p.profile_id, unit);
                let mut d = DeviceInstance::from_profile(&id, &format!("{} (simulated)", p.model.get("en")), &link, &p);
                d.unit_id = unit;
                d.response_timeout_ms = Some(300);
                s.add_device(d).map_err(err)?;
                ids.push(id);
            }
            if let [soil, vfd, temp] = ids.as_slice() {
                for a in alarm_presets(soil, vfd, temp) {
                    s.alarm_add(a).map_err(err)?;
                }
            }
            s.start_polling(TRAINING_LINK_ID).map_err(err)?;
        }
    }
    Ok(training_status(state))
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct FaultReq {
    unit: u8,
    fault: TrainingFault,
    seconds: u32,
}

/// Fault injection exists only on the training bus (it acts on the simulator world).
#[tauri::command]
pub fn training_fault(state: State<'_, AppState>, req: FaultReq) -> R<TrainingStatus> {
    let t = training_of(&state).ok_or("Training mode is not started")?;
    t.inject(req.unit, req.fault, u64::from(req.seconds) * 1000)
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    Ok(training_status(state))
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn training_clear(state: State<'_, AppState>, unit: u8) -> R<TrainingStatus> {
    let t = training_of(&state).ok_or("Training mode is not started")?;
    t.clear(unit);
    Ok(training_status(state))
}

//! `Control`: what the app shell calls for control, commissioning and process
//! feedback (commissioning-control design §2–§5). It owns the one
//! `CommandService` of the app and talks to devices only through the link
//! worker's queue (`Session::command_access`).
//!
//! Every call first checks the armed link's generation: a disconnect,
//! reconnect, link loss or settings change since arming drops the arm, and
//! nothing resumes on its own (safety rules 3 and 6).

use super::audit::AuditEvent;
use super::commission::{CommSettings, StepError, Wizard, WizardStep};
use super::feedback::{FeedbackWatch, Observation};
use super::{
    Ack, CommSettingKind, CommandConfig, CommandError, CommandLink, CommandOutcome, CommandRequest, CommandService,
    CommandState, CommandTarget, DisarmReason, Operator, Preview, Readback, Role,
};
use crate::profile::CapabilityLevel;
use crate::protocol::pdu::ReadRequest;
use crate::session::{LinkState, Session, SessionError};
use serde::Serialize;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, MutexGuard};
use thiserror::Error;

#[derive(Debug, Error, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum ControlError {
    #[error(transparent)]
    Command(#[from] CommandError),
    #[error(transparent)]
    Session(#[from] SessionError),
    #[error(transparent)]
    Step(#[from] StepError),
    #[error("{0}")]
    Rejected(String),
}

/// The last command: its preview, outcome and process feedback, kept for the panel.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize)]
pub struct LastCommand {
    pub preview: Preview,
    pub sent: bool,
    pub outcome: Option<CommandOutcome>,
    pub feedback: Option<FeedbackWatch>,
    #[serde(skip)]
    target: Option<CommandTarget>,
    #[serde(skip)]
    operator: Option<Operator>,
    #[serde(skip)]
    feedback_logged: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize)]
pub struct ControlStatus {
    pub state: CommandState,
    pub armed_device: Option<String>,
    pub armed_user: Option<String>,
    pub armed_role: Option<Role>,
    pub armed_remaining_ms: Option<u64>,
    pub arm_timeout_ms: u64,
    /// Why the last arm ended (shown once the panel notices).
    pub disarm_reason: Option<DisarmReason>,
    pub last: Option<LastCommand>,
    pub wizard: Option<Wizard>,
}

struct Inner {
    svc: CommandService,
    armed_link: Option<(String, u64)>,
    disarm_reason: Option<DisarmReason>,
    last: Option<LastCommand>,
    wizard: Option<Wizard>,
    wizard_target: Option<(CommandTarget, Operator)>,
}

pub struct Control {
    session: Arc<Session>,
    inner: Mutex<Inner>,
}

fn reason_for(state: Option<LinkState>, same_generation: bool) -> DisarmReason {
    match state {
        None | Some(LinkState::Disconnected) => DisarmReason::Disconnect,
        Some(LinkState::Down) => DisarmReason::LinkLost,
        Some(_) if !same_generation => DisarmReason::Reconnect,
        // Polling stopped by the user: the bus is no longer owned by a worker.
        Some(_) => DisarmReason::Disconnect,
    }
}

impl Control {
    pub fn new(session: Arc<Session>, config: CommandConfig) -> Self {
        let svc = CommandService::new(session.clock(), session.audit_sink(), session.session_id(), config);
        Self {
            session,
            inner: Mutex::new(Inner {
                svc,
                armed_link: None,
                disarm_reason: None,
                last: None,
                wizard: None,
                wizard_target: None,
            }),
        }
    }

    fn lock(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, Inner> {
        self.inner.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
    }

    /// Drop the arm when the link changed since arming, or when its idle time ran out.
    fn check(&self, g: &mut Inner) {
        if let Some((link, gen_at_arm)) = g.armed_link.clone() {
            let now = self.session.link_generation(&link);
            let ok = now.is_some_and(|(gen_now, st)| gen_now == gen_at_arm && st == LinkState::Polling);
            if !ok {
                let reason = reason_for(now.map(|n| n.1), now.is_some_and(|n| n.0 == gen_at_arm));
                g.svc.disarm(reason);
                g.armed_link = None;
                g.disarm_reason = Some(reason);
            }
        }
        if g.armed_link.is_some() && g.svc.expire_if_due() {
            g.armed_link = None;
            g.disarm_reason = Some(DisarmReason::Expired);
        }
        if g.svc.armed_device().is_none() {
            if g.armed_link.is_some() && g.disarm_reason.is_none() {
                // Dropped inside the service: idle expiry, or link loss during a send.
                let lost = g
                    .last
                    .as_ref()
                    .and_then(|l| l.outcome.as_ref())
                    .is_some_and(|o| matches!(o.ack, Ack::LinkLost | Ack::NotSent));
                g.disarm_reason = Some(if lost {
                    DisarmReason::LinkLost
                } else {
                    DisarmReason::Expired
                });
            }
            g.armed_link = None;
        }
    }

    fn evaluate_feedback(&self, g: &mut Inner) {
        let Some(last) = g.last.as_mut() else { return };
        let Some(w) = last.feedback.as_mut() else { return };
        if last.feedback_logged {
            return;
        }
        let now = self.session.clock().utc_ms();
        let obs = self.session.tag(&w.device_id, &w.register).map(|t| Observation {
            ts_ms: t.ts_ms,
            good: t.quality == "GOOD",
            value: if w.bit.is_some() {
                t.raw.as_ref().and_then(|r| r.first()).map(|v| f64::from(*v))
            } else {
                t.value
            },
        });
        let st = w.observe(obs, now);
        if st.is_final() {
            last.feedback_logged = true;
            let w = w.clone();
            let (Some(target), Some(op)) = (last.target.clone(), last.operator.clone()) else {
                return;
            };
            let preview_id = last.preview.id;
            let command_id = last.preview.command_id.clone();
            // Best effort: the command already happened; a failed row shows in the historian error.
            let _ = g.svc.note(AuditEvent::Feedback, &target, &op, |r| {
                r.preview_id = Some(preview_id);
                r.command_id = command_id;
                r.register_id = Some(w.register.clone());
                r.requested_value = Some(w.target);
                r.readback_value = w.last_value;
                r.readback = Some(st.as_str().into());
                r.note = Some(format!(
                    "process feedback {} (target {} ± {}, {} ms window)",
                    st.as_str(),
                    w.target,
                    w.tolerance,
                    w.deadline_ms - w.started_ms
                ));
            });
        }
    }

    pub fn status(&self) -> ControlStatus {
        let mut g = self.lock();
        self.check(&mut g);
        self.evaluate_feedback(&mut g);
        ControlStatus {
            state: g.svc.state(),
            armed_device: g.svc.armed_device().map(str::to_owned),
            armed_user: g.svc.armed_operator().map(|o| o.user.clone()),
            armed_role: g.svc.armed_operator().map(|o| o.role),
            armed_remaining_ms: g.svc.armed_remaining_ms(),
            arm_timeout_ms: g.svc.arm_timeout_ms(),
            disarm_reason: g.disarm_reason,
            last: g.last.clone(),
            wizard: g.wizard.clone(),
        }
    }

    pub fn arm(&self, device_id: &str, user: &str, role: Role) -> Result<ControlStatus, ControlError> {
        let user = user.trim();
        if user.is_empty() || user.chars().count() > 64 || user.chars().any(char::is_control) {
            return Err(ControlError::Rejected("enter a user name (1-64 characters)".into()));
        }
        {
            let mut g = self.lock();
            self.check(&mut g);
            let access = self.session.command_access(device_id)?;
            let link = access.target.link.id.clone();
            g.svc.arm(
                access.target,
                Operator {
                    user: user.to_owned(),
                    role,
                },
            )?;
            g.armed_link = Some((link, access.generation));
            g.disarm_reason = None;
        }
        Ok(self.status())
    }

    pub fn disarm(&self, reason: DisarmReason) -> ControlStatus {
        {
            let mut g = self.lock();
            if g.svc.armed_device().is_some() {
                g.svc.disarm(reason);
                g.disarm_reason = Some(reason);
            }
            g.armed_link = None;
        }
        self.status()
    }

    fn armed_access(
        &self,
        g: &mut Inner,
        device_id: &str,
    ) -> Result<crate::session::access::CommandAccess, ControlError> {
        self.check(g);
        let Some(armed) = g.svc.armed_device().map(str::to_owned) else {
            return Err(CommandError::NotArmed.into());
        };
        if armed != device_id {
            return Err(CommandError::WrongDevice {
                armed,
                requested: device_id.to_owned(),
            }
            .into());
        }
        let access = self.session.command_access(device_id)?;

//! `Control`: what the app shell calls for control, commissioning and process
//! feedback (commissioning-control design §2–§5). It owns the one
//! `CommandService` of the app and talks to devices only through the link
//! worker's queue (`Session::command_access`).
//!
//! Every call first checks the armed link's generation: a disconnect,
//! reconnect, link loss or settings change since arming drops the arm, and
//! nothing resumes on its own (safety rules 3 and 6).

use super::audit::AuditEvent;
use super::commission::{CommSettings, StepError, Wizard, WizardStep};
use super::feedback::{FeedbackWatch, Observation};
use super::{
    Ack, CommSettingKind, CommandConfig, CommandError, CommandLink, CommandOutcome, CommandRequest, CommandService,
    CommandState, CommandTarget, DisarmReason, Operator, Preview, Readback, Role,
};
use crate::profile::CapabilityLevel;
use crate::protocol::pdu::ReadRequest;
use crate::session::{LinkState, Session, SessionError};
use serde::Serialize;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, MutexGuard};
use thiserror::Error;

#[derive(Debug, Error, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum ControlError {
    #[error(transparent)]
    Command(#[from] CommandError),
    #[error(transparent)]
    Session(#[from] SessionError),
    #[error(transparent)]
    Step(#[from] StepError),
    #[error("{0}")]
    Rejected(String),
}

/// The last command: its preview, outcome and process feedback, kept for the panel.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize)]
pub struct LastCommand {
    pub preview: Preview,
    pub sent: bool,
    pub outcome: Option<CommandOutcome>,
    pub feedback: Option<FeedbackWatch>,
    #[serde(skip)]
    target: Option<CommandTarget>,
    #[serde(skip)]
    operator: Option<Operator>,
    #[serde(skip)]
    feedback_logged: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize)]
pub struct ControlStatus {
    pub state: CommandState,
    pub armed_device: Option<String>,
    pub armed_user: Option<String>,
    pub armed_role: Option<Role>,
    pub armed_remaining_ms: Option<u64>,
    pub arm_timeout_ms: u64,
    /// Why the last arm ended (shown once the panel notices).
    pub disarm_reason: Option<DisarmReason>,
    pub last: Option<LastCommand>,
    pub wizard: Option<Wizard>,
}

struct Inner {
    svc: CommandService,
    armed_link: Option<(String, u64)>,
    disarm_reason: Option<DisarmReason>,
    last: Option<LastCommand>,
    wizard: Option<Wizard>,
    wizard_target: Option<(CommandTarget, Operator)>,
}

pub struct Control {
    session: Arc<Session>,
    inner: Mutex<Inner>,
}

fn reason_for(state: Option<LinkState>, same_generation: bool) -> DisarmReason {
    match state {
        None | Some(LinkState::Disconnected) => DisarmReason::Disconnect,
        Some(LinkState::Down) => DisarmReason::LinkLost,
        Some(_) if !same_generation => DisarmReason::Reconnect,
        // Polling stopped by the user: the bus is no longer owned by a worker.
        Some(_) => DisarmReason::Disconnect,
    }
}

    pub fn new(session: Arc<Session>, config: CommandConfig) -> Self {
        let svc = CommandService::new(session.clock(), session.audit_sink(), session.session_id(), config);
        Self {
            session,
            inner: Mutex::new(Inner {
                svc,
                armed_link: None,
                disarm_reason: None,
                last: None,
                wizard: None,
                wizard_target: None,
            }),
        }
    }

    fn lock(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, Inner> {
        self.inner.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
    }

    /// Drop the arm when the link changed since arming, or when its idle time ran out.
    fn check(&self, g: &mut Inner) {
        if let Some((link, gen_at_arm)) = g.armed_link.clone() {
            let now = self.session.link_generation(&link);
            let ok = now.is_some_and(|(gen_now, st)| gen_now == gen_at_arm && st == LinkState::Polling);
            if !ok {
                let reason = reason_for(now.map(|n| n.1), now.is_some_and(|n| n.0 == gen_at_arm));

            let w = w.clone();
            let (Some(target), Some(op)) = (last.target.clone(), last.operator.clone()) else {

                r.command_id = command_id;
                r.register_id = Some(w.register.clone());
                r.requested_value = Some(w.target);
                r.readback_value = w.last_value;
                r.readback = Some(st.as_str().into());

                    w.deadline_ms - w.started_ms

            arm_timeout_ms: g.svc.arm_timeout_ms(),

            return Err(ControlError::Rejected("enter a user name (1-64 characters)".into()));
        }
        {
            let mut g = self.lock();
            self.check(&mut g);
            let access = self.session.command_access(device_id)?;
            let link = access.target.link.id.clone();
            g.svc.arm(
                access.target,

    (a - b).abs() <= 1e-9 * a.abs().max(b.abs()).max(1.0)
}

fn check_bounds(reg: &Register, value: f64) -> Result<(), CommandError> {
    if !value.is_finite() {
        return Err(CommandError::OutOfBounds("value is not a finite number".into()));
    }
    let Some(w) = &reg.write else {
        return Err(CommandError::NotWritable(reg.id.clone()));
    };
    if let Some(allowed) = &w.allowed_values {
        if !allowed.iter().any(|a| same_value(*a, value)) {
            return Err(CommandError::OutOfBounds(format!("{value} is not one of {allowed:?}")));
        }
    } else if let (Some(min), Some(max)) = (w.min, w.max) {
        if value < min || value > max {
            return Err(CommandError::OutOfBounds(format!("{value} is outside {min}..{max}")));
        }
        if let Some(step) = w.step {
            let k = (value - min) / step;
            if (k - k.round()).abs() > 1e-6 {
                return Err(CommandError::OutOfBounds(format!(
                    "{value} is not a multiple of {step} from {min}"
                )));
            }
        }
    } else if reg.table == Table::Coil {
        if value != 0.0 && value != 1.0 {
            return Err(CommandError::OutOfBounds("a coil takes 0 or 1".into()));
        }
    } else {
        return Err(CommandError::OutOfBounds("the profile gives no write bounds".into()));
    }
    if let Some([lo, hi]) = reg.valid_range
        && (value < lo || value > hi)
    {
        return Err(CommandError::OutOfBounds(format!(
            "{value} is outside the valid range {lo}..{hi}"
        )));
    }
    Ok(())
}

    }

    pub fn arm(&mut self, target: CommandTarget, operator: Operator) -> Result<(), CommandError> {
        if matches!(self.inner, Inner::Sent | Inner::ReadBack) {
            return Err(CommandError::WrongState {

        let rec = self.base_record(AuditEvent::Arm);
        if let Err(e) = self.audit.append(&rec) {
            self.armed = None;
            return Err(e.into());
        }
        self.inner = Inner::Armed;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Drop arming (operator, disconnect, reconnect, profile change, app background).
    pub fn disarm(&mut self, reason: DisarmReason) {
        if self.armed.is_none() {
            self.inner = Inner::Idle;
            return;
        }
        let mut rec = self.base_record(AuditEvent::Disarm);
        rec.note = Some(reason.as_str().into());
        let _ = self.audit.append(&rec);
        self.armed = None;
        self.inner = Inner::Idle;
    }

    /// Drop a preview or confirmation without sending.
    pub fn cancel(&mut self) -> Result<(), CommandError> {
        match std::mem::replace(&mut self.inner, Inner::Armed) {
            Inner::Previewed(plan) | Inner::Confirmed(plan) => {
                let rec = self.plan_record(AuditEvent::Cancel, &plan.preview);
                let _ = self.audit.append(&rec);

                    self.inner = Inner::Idle;
                }

            }
            other => {
                let actual = matches!(other, Inner::Idle);
                self.inner = other;
                if actual { Err(CommandError::NotArmed) } else { Ok(()) }
            }
        }
    }

//! The read-only HTTP surface (safety rule 15). Every route is GET, every request
//! passes the same guard (rate limit, token, no body, GET only), and nothing here
//! can reach the command service, the poll workers or a transport.

use super::hub::Hub;
use super::limits::{Limiter, Verdict};
use super::token=<redacted> super::{AssetSource, LanSource, TrendFail};
use axum::Router;
use axum::body::Body;
use axum::extract::ws::{CloseFrame, Message, Utf8Bytes, WebSocket, WebSocketUpgrade};
use axum::extract::{Extension, Query, Request, State};
use axum::http::{HeaderMap, HeaderValue, Method, StatusCode, Uri, header};
use axum::middleware::{self, Next};
use axum::response::Response;
use axum::routing::get;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::net::SocketAddr;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, MutexGuard};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
use tokio::sync::{broadcast, watch};

/// What a route does. The router is built from [`ROUTES`], so the table is the whole surface.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Kind {
    Index,
    Snapshot,
    Trend,
    Stream,
}

/// Every route of the server. All GET. Other paths fall through to the static
/// files of the frontend build (also GET only, also behind the token).
pub const ROUTES: &[(&str, &str, Kind)] = &[
    ("/", "GET", Kind::Index),
    ("/api/snapshot", "GET", Kind::Snapshot),
    ("/api/trend", "GET", Kind::Trend),
    ("/api/stream", "GET", Kind::Stream),

    let ctx = Arc::clone(&guard.ctx);
    let mut shutdown = ctx.shutdown.clone();
    let (snap, mut rx) = ctx.hub.snapshot_and_subscribe();
    if !send(&mut socket, &snap).await {

    loop {
        tokio::select! {
            frame = rx.recv() => match frame {
                Ok(text) => {
                    if !send(&mut socket, &text).await { break; }

                    // Never skip silently: say so, then resend the whole state.
                    let note = super::hub::message("lagged", &missed);

                    rx = fresh;
                    if !send(&mut socket, &note).await || !send(&mut socket, &snap).await { break; }

            incoming = socket.recv() => match incoming {
                None | Some(Err(_)) | Some(Ok(Message::Close(_))) => break,

            _ = shutdown.changed() => {
                let _ = socket.send(Message::Close(Some(CloseFrame { code: 1001, reason: Utf8Bytes::from_static("server stopped") }))).await;

            }
        }
    }
